title: Language profile
description: How one language writes the model's types, collections, nullability and names (rules.md, Language profiles).

types.description: Each Intent primitive to the type names that mean it in code, simple or qualified

collections.description: Forms meaning a collection of T: List<T>, T[]

void.description: true: the wrapper without T means no result, as C#'s Task
Return types meaning a function returns nothing, as Python's None

suffix.description: As C#'s ?, in a nullable context for reference types

boxed.description: A primitive to its boxed type, which is nullable: int to Integer

notStated.description: Why the language leaves a type's nullability unstated, and how to make it checkable: the engine/notStated note's text

untyped.description: Present when the language lets a declaration leave its type out (JavaScript, TypeScript's inferred types, unannotated Python): a type claim on one is can't verify, unresolved, and listed in an engine/notStated note, never a finding of its own

notStated.description: Why the code leaves these types out, and how to make them checkable: the engine/notStated note's text

naming.description: From an element's name to a name in code: {Name} with the placeholder filters ({Name|camel}). A kind with no pattern is named as modelled.

interface.description: A type the conventions allow only as an interface, as C#'s I{Name}; defaults to type

accessors.description: The methods that read or write a field, as Java's get{Name|pascal}: unmodelled.member doesn't report a located field's accessors
